sections.english: At break of day, when you are reluctant to get up, have this thought ready to mind: 'I am getting up for a man's work. Do I still then resent it, if I am going out to do what I was born for, the purpose for which I was brought into the world? Or was I created to wrap myself in blankets and keep warm?' 'But this is more pleasant.' Were you then born for pleasure — all for feeling, not for action? Can you not see plants, birds, ants, spiders, bees all doing their own work, each helping in their own way to order the world? And then you do not want to do the work of a human being — you do not hurry to the demands of your own nature. 'But one needs rest too.' One does indeed: I agree. But nature has set limits to this too, just as it has to eating and drinking, and yet you go beyond these limits, beyond what you need. Not in your actions, though, not any longer: here you stay below your capability. The point is that you do not love yourself — otherwise you would love both your own nature and her purpose for you. Other men love their own pursuit and absorb themselves in its performance to the exclusion of bath and food: but you have less regard for your own nature than the smith has for his metal-work, the dancer for his dancing, the money-grubber for his money, the exhibitionist for his little moment of fame. Yet these people, when impassioned, give up food and sleep for the promotion of their pursuits: and you think social action less important, less worthy of effort?
sections.chinese: 拂晓之际，你若不情愿起身，当备此念于心中：「我起身为人之事业。若我去做我生而为之的事、那因之而被带入这世界的目的，我尚且抱怨吗？抑或我之被造，乃是为了裹身毛毯、保持温暖？」「可那样更舒适。」难道你是为逸乐而生——一切皆为感受，不为行动？你难道不曾看见花草、飞鸟、蚂蚁、蜘蛛、蜜蜂，皆各行己务，各以其道襄助世界之秩序？而你竟不想做一个人之工作——你竟不急急奔赴你自身本性之要求。「可是人也需要休息。」确实需要：我同意。然而自然于此也设了界限，正如于饮食一般，可是你却逾越了这些界限，超出了你之所需要。但在行动方面，你却不是这样、不再是这样：在此你停留在能力之下。其要点在于：你不爱你自己——否则你便会既爱自己之本然天性，也爱她为你所设之目的。他人热爱己之志业，沉醉于其施行之中，至于废寝忘食、不浴不沐：而你对于自己之本然天性，尚不如铁匠之珍视其金工、舞者之珍视其舞艺、财迷之珍视其金钱、好名之徒珍视他那片刻之浮名。然而，此等之人，当其热情激发之时，宁弃饮食与睡眠以推进其志业：而你却以为社会性行动较不重要、较不值得付出努力？

sections.english: How easy it is to drive away or obliterate from one's mind every impression which is troublesome or alien, and then to be immediately in perfect calm.
sections.chinese: 驱逐一己心中一切烦扰与格格不入之印象，随即安处于全然平静——这是何其轻易之事。

sections.english: Judge yourself entitled to any word or action which is in accord with nature, and do not let any subsequent criticism or persuasion from anyone talk you out of it. No, if it was a good thing to do or say, do not revoke your entitlement. Those others are guided by their own minds and pursue their own impulses. Do not be distracted by any of this, but continue straight ahead, following your own nature and universal nature: these two have one and the same path.
sections.chinese: 凡有言行合乎自然，便当你认自己有权为之，且勿令日后任何人之批评或劝说劝退了你。不，若那曾是好事、好话，便不要撤消你于此事之权。彼等别人各由其己之心所导引，各追逐己之冲动。你不必为其中任何一事而分心，但继续直前，追随你自己之本然与宇宙之本然：此二者共享同一道路。

sections.english: I travel on by nature's path until I fall and find rest, breathing my last into that air from which I draw my daily breath, and falling on that earth which gave my father his seed, my mother her blood, my nurse her milk; the earth which for so many years has fed and watered me day by day; the earth which bears my tread and all the ways in which I abuse her.
sections.chinese: 我循自然之道前行，直至倒下而得安息——呼出最后一息入于那我日日呼吸其间的空气，倒在那给我父亲精种、给我母亲血液、给我乳母乳汁的大地之上；那大地多年来日复一日供我饮食；那大地承载我之践踏，以及我一如等闲折磨她的种种方式。

sections.english: They cannot admire you for intellect. Granted — but there are many other qualities of which you cannot say, 'but that is not the way I am made'. So display those virtues which are wholly in your own power — integrity, dignity, hard work, self-denial, contentment, frugality, kindness, independence, simplicity, discretion, magnanimity. Do you not see how many virtues you can already display without any excuse of lack of talent or aptitude? And yet you are still content to lag behind. Or does the fact that you have no inborn talent oblige you to grumble, to scrimp, to toady, to blame your poor body, to suck up, to brag, to have your mind in such turmoil? No, by heaven, it does not! You could have got rid of all this long ago, and only be charged — if charge there is — with being rather slow and dull of comprehension. And yet even this can be worked on — unless you ignore or welcome your stupidity.
sections.chinese: 他们不能因才智而钦慕你。承认便是——但还有许多其他品质，你不能说，「我天生不是那样」。所以，展现那些全在你权能之内的美德——正直、尊严、勤勉、克己、知足、俭朴、仁善、独立、素朴、审慎、恢宏大度。难道你看不见你已能展现如此众多之美德，而无需以欠缺天赋或天资为借口？而你却依然甘心落于后头。抑或，你没有天赋，便非得要牢骚满腹、一钱如命、谄媚讨好、怪责你这可怜的躯体、阿谀奉迎、虚夸自吹、使你之心如此纷扰不宁？不，苍天为证，并非这般！你早该已久弃此一切，唯一可能之责难——若真有何责难——不过是说你理解较慢较钝。而即便是此，也可加以修炼——除你忽视或欢迎你自己的愚蠢。

sections.english: One sort of person, when he has done a kindness to another, is quick also to chalk up the return due to him. A second is not so quick in that way, but even so he privately thinks of the other as his debtor, and is well aware of what he has done. A third sort is in a way not even conscious of his action, but is like the vine which has produced grapes and looks for nothing else once it has borne its own fruit. A horse that has raced, a dog that has tracked, a bee that has made honey, and a man that has done good — none of these knows what they have done, but they pass on to the next action, just as the vine passes on to bear grapes again in due season. So you ought to be one of those who, in a sense, are unconscious of the good they do.
sections.chinese: 有一种人，对别人施了善举后，很快也记下该得之回报。第二种人没有那么快疾，但私心里仍视对方为自己之负债者，且十分清楚自己所做之事。第三种人则在某种方式上甚至意识不到自己所行之善，就像那结了葡萄的藤蔓，一旦结了果实之后便不再期盼任何别物。赛跑过的马，追踪过的犬，酿了蜜的蜂，施了善的人——此中无一知晓自己做了什么，只是径自转入下一个行动，就像藤蔓径自在合宜时节再次结出葡萄。因此，你应当成为那种在某种意义上对自己所行之善毫无知觉的人。

sections.english: A prayer of the Athenian people: 'Rain, rain, dear Zeus, on the cornland and the plain of Attica.' Prayer should be thus simple and open, or not at all. Just as it is commonly said that Asclepius has prescribed someone horse-riding, or cold baths, or walking barefoot, so we could say that the nature of the Whole has prescribed him disease, disablement, loss, or any other such affliction. In the first case 'prescribed' means something like this: 'ordered this course for this person as conducive to his health'. In the second the meaning is that what happens to each individual is somehow arranged to conduce to his destiny.
sections.chinese: 雅典人有一句祈祷：「降雨，降雨，亲爱的宙斯，降在谷田与阿提卡平原之上吧。」祈祷当如是简单而开阔，否则便不若无。正如人常说阿斯克勒庇俄斯给某人开了骑马、冷水浴或赤足行走之方子，我们同样可以说，宇宙整体之自然给某人开了疾病、残障、丧损，或任何其他类似之苦楚。在前一种情形，「开方」之意约略若此：「为此人规定此一疗程，以便有益于他的健康。」在后一种情形，其意乃是：每一人所遭逢之事，均被以某种方式安排得有益于他的命运。

sections.english: So there are two reasons why you should be content with your experience. One is that this has happened to you, was prescribed for you, and is related to you, a thread of destiny spun for you from the first by the most ancient causes. The second is that what comes to each individual is a determining part of the welfare, the perfection, and indeed the very coherence of that which governs the Whole. Because the complete Whole is maimed if you sever even the tiniest fraction of its connection and continuity: this is true of its constituent parts, and true likewise of its causes. And you do sever something, to the extent that you can, whenever you fret at your lot: this is, in a sense, a destruction.
sections.chinese: 如此，你有两条理由当于你之所历心满意足。其一，此事已临到你身，是为你所开的方子，与你密切相关，乃自最初由最古远之诸因为你纺出的一条命运之线。其二，临到每一个体者，乃是那统御宇宙整体者之福祉、完美，乃至其实恰连贯性中的一个决定性部分。因为完整的整体，你若切断其联结与连续之哪怕最微弱的一丝，也将残缺：此理对于其组成部分为真，对于其原因亦同样为真。而你每当你为自己之遭际烦躁不宁时，便在你力所能及之范围内，切断了某物：这在某种意义上，乃是一种毁坏。

sections.english: Do not give up in disgust or impatience if you do not find action on the right principles consolidated into a habit in all that you do. No: if you have taken a fall, come back again, and be glad if most of your actions are on the right side of humanity. And love what you return to. Do not come back to philosophy as schoolboy to tutor, but rather as a man with ophthalmia returns to his sponge and salve, or another to his poultice or lotion. In this way you will prove that obedience to reason is no great burden, but a source of relief. Remember too that philosophy wants only what your nature wants: whereas you were wanting something unnatural to you. Now what could be more agreeable than the needs of your own nature?
sections.chinese: 若你未能发现依正确原则之行事在你的全部作为中巩固为习惯，不要厌恶地或焦躁地放弃。不：若你跌倒了，便再回来，若你的大多数行为是在人之正道上，便该高兴。且爱那重归之处。勿如学童之回到塾师面前那样回到哲学，而当如患眼疾之人回到他的海绵和药膏，或另一人回到他之敷剂或洗液。如此，你便证明了听从理性并非巨大负担，反是一种宽释之来源。也要记得，哲学所要的，无非是你本性所要的；而你却一直在要那不合你本性的东西。有什么能比你自身本性之需要更为宜人？

sections.english: Realities are wrapped in such a veil (as it were) that several philosophers of distinction have thought them altogether beyond comprehension, while even the Stoics think them hard to comprehend. And every assent we may give to our perceptions is fallible: the infallible man does not exist. Pass, then, to the very objects of our experience — how short-lived they are, how shoddy: a catamite, a whore, a thief could own them. Go on now to the characters of your fellows: it is hard to tolerate even the best of them, not to speak of one's difficulty in enduring even oneself. In all this murk and dirt, in all this flux of being, time, movement, things moved, I cannot begin to see what on earth there is to value or even to aim for. Rather the opposite: one should console oneself with the anticipation of natural release, not impatient of its delay, but taking comfort in just these two thoughts. One, that nothing will happen to me which is not in accordance with the nature of the Whole: the other, that it is in my control to do nothing contrary to my god and the divinity within me — no one can force me to this offence.
sections.chinese: 事物之真相笼罩在如此一层幕纱之中（可如是说），以至若干卓著之哲学家曾认为它们全然不可知解，而即便是斯多亚学派也认其为难以知解。而我们给予每一感知之同意，皆可能犯错：无误之人，世间并无。那么，转向我们经验之具体对象吧——看它们何其短寿、何其粗劣：一娈童、一娼妓、一盗贼，也能拥有它们。再进而看看你同侪之品格：即便是最优秀者，也难忍耐，更不用说人欲忍受一己之困难了。在此一切昏暗与污秽中，在此存在、时间、运动、被移之物之一切流转中，我实在看不出到底有什么值得珍视、甚至值得求取。恰恰相反：人当以对自然解脱之期待来宽慰自己，不为其延迟而焦躁，而在此仅有的两个念头中取慰。其一，凡临到我身之一切，皆与宇宙整体之本性相合；其二，我能掌控自己不做任何违逆我之守护神与内里之神性之事——无人能强使我犯此过错。

sections.english: To what use, then, am I now putting my soul? Ask yourself this question on every occasion. Examine yourself. 'What do I now have in this part of me called the directing mind? What sort of soul do I have after all? Is it that of a child? A boy? A woman? A despot? A beast of the field? A wild animal?'
sections.chinese: 那么，我此刻正将我的灵魂用于何种用途？每一场合都以此问诘问自身。审察你自己。「我此刻在我身中那称为主导心灵的部分中有着什么？我究竟有着何种灵魂？是一孩童的灵魂？一男孩的？一妇人的？一暴君的？一田间牲畜的？一野兽的？」

sections.english: Here is a way to understand what sort of things the majority take to be 'goods'. If you think of the true goods there are — wisdom, for example, self-control, justice, courage — with these in your mind you could not give any credence to the popular saying of 'too many goods to make room', because it will not apply. But bearing in mind what the majority see as goods you will hear and readily accept what the comic poet says as a fair comment.
sections.chinese: 有一种方式可理解大多数人视为「好」的究竟是何种东西。你若思想那真正的诸般善好——譬如智慧、自制、正义、勇气——心中怀着这些，你便不可能对那通俗之谚语「好东西太多，无处可容」给予任何认可，因为它根本不适用。然而，若你心中所想的是大多数人眼中的诸般好物，你便会听到喜剧诗人之语，并欣然认同其为一公允之评论。

sections.english: I am made up of the causal and the material. Neither of these will disappear into nothing, just as neither came to be out of nothing. So every part of me will be assigned its changed place in some part of the universe, and that will change again into another part of the universe, and so on to infinity. A similar sequence of change brought me into existence, and my parents before me, and so back in another infinity of regression.
sections.chinese: 我由因果与物质之两种所构成。此二者皆不会消逝于虚无，正如其皆非由虚无产生。故我之每一部分将被分配其变化之后的、宇宙某处之位置，而后又将变成宇宙之另一部分，如此以至无穷。相似的变化序列使我得以存在，我之父母亦先于我而如此，如此追溯，亦是另一重无穷之回退。

sections.english: Reason and the art of reasoning are faculties self-determined by their own nature and their own products. They start from the relevant premise and follow the path to the proposed end. That is why acts of reason are called 'right' acts, signifying the rightness of the path thus followed.
sections.chinese: 理性与推理之术，乃是由其自身本性与自身产物所自行决定的官能。它们从相应之前提出发，沿道而行直至所设定之目的。这便是为何理性之行为被称为「正确」之行为，表明由此而循之道的正确性。

sections.english: One should pay no attention to any of those things which do not belong to man's portion incumbent on him as a human being. They are not demanded of a man; man's nature does not proclaim them; they are not consummations of that nature. Therefore they do not constitute man's end either, nor yet any means to that end — that is, good.
sections.chinese: 对于那些不属于人之份内——作为一个人之为人的身分所当担之份——的任何事物，皆不当留意。它们并非对人有所要求；人之本性并不宣告它们；它们亦非彼本性之完满成就。故此，它们既不构成人之目的，亦不作任何导向彼目的之手段——即所谓善好。

sections.english: Your mind will take on the character of your most frequent thoughts: souls are dyed by thoughts. So dye your own with a succession of thoughts like these. For example: where life can be lived, so can a good life; but life can be lived in a palace; therefore a good life can be lived in a palace. Again: each creature is made in the interest of another; its course is directed to that for which it was made; its end lies in that to which its course is directed; and where its end is, there also for each is its benefit and its good. It follows that the good of a rational creature is community.
sections.chinese: 你的心灵将染上你最频繁之思想的品性：灵魂被思想所浸染。那便以一系列如下的思想浸染你自己的心灵。例如：生命可在何处活出，善好的生命便可同样活出；而生命可活于宫廷之中；故此，善好的生命也可活于宫廷之中。又如：每类造物皆为另一类之利益而被造；其所行之途指向其被造之目的；其终点就在其途所指之处；而何处有终点，便也是每类造物之利益和善好所在之处。由此可推：理性造物之善好，即是共同体。

sections.english: To pursue the impossible is madness: and it is impossible for bad men not to act in character.
sections.chinese: 追求不可能之事，乃是疯狂；而恶人不按本性与品格行事，是绝不可能的。

sections.english: Nothing happens to any creature beyond its own natural endurance. Another has the same experience as you: either through failure to recognize what has happened to him, or in a display of courage, he remains calm and untroubled. Strange, then, that ignorance and pretension should be stronger than wisdom.
sections.chinese: 凡所发生，无一超出任何造物自身自然之承受力。他人有与你相同之经历：要么出于未能辨识所发生于己之事，要么出于所展现之勇毅，他保持平静，不为所扰。然而奇怪的是，无知与虚张声势竟比智慧更有力量。

sections.english: Things of themselves cannot touch the soul at all. They have no entry to the soul, and cannot turn or move it. The soul alone turns and moves itself, making all externals presented to it cohere with the judgements it thinks worthy of itself.
sections.chinese: 物之本身丝毫不能触及灵魂。它们无由进入灵魂，亦不能转动或移易它。灵魂独自转动并移易自己，令一切呈现于它面前之外物，与它所思为配得上自己的判断相协一致。

sections.english: In one respect man is something with the closest affinity to us, in that it is our duty to do good to men and tolerate them. But in so far as some are obstacles to my proper work, man joins the category of things indifferent to me — no less than the sun, the wind, a wild animal. These can impede some activity, yes, but they form no impediments to my impulse or my disposition, because here there is conditional commitment and the power of adaptation. The mind adapts and turns round any obstacle to action to serve its objective: a hindrance to a given work is turned to its furtherance, an obstacle in a given path becomes an advance.
sections.chinese: 就一方面而言，人与我们最相亲近，因我们当有行善于人、容耐于人之职责。然而，就某些人是阻碍我正当工作之障碍而言，人便落入于我而言漠不相干之物的范畴——不异于太阳、风、野兽。此等物可阻碍某种活动，诚然，但并不对我的冲动或我的性情构成障碍，因为此处有的是有条件之投入与调适之能力。心灵将任何行动之障碍调适并转而成全其目标：一给定工作之阻碍便被转为推动，一给定道路上之障碍便成了前行。

sections.english: Revere the ultimate power in the universe: this is what makes use of all things and directs all things. But similarly revere the ultimate power in yourself: this is akin to that other power. In you too this is what makes use of all else, and your life is governed by it.
sections.chinese: 敬畏那宇宙中至高之力：那即是运用万物、引导万物者。同样，也敬畏你自身中至高之力：此力与彼另一力血脉相通。在你之内，这也同样是用及一切其他之物者，你的生命便受其主宰。

sections.english: What is not harmful to the city does not harm the citizen either. Whenever you imagine you have been harmed, apply this criterion: if the city is not harmed by this, then I have not been harmed either. If on the other hand harm is done to the city, you should not be angry, but demonstrate to the doer of this harm what he has failed to see himself.
sections.chinese: 于城邦无害之事，亦不害于公民。每当你想象自己受了伤害，便运用此一标尺：若城邦未因此受伤害，那么我也不曾受伤害。另一方面，若伤害确然加于城邦，你不当愤怒，而当向此伤害之行施者，明示他所未能自见之过。

sections.english: Reflect often on the speed with which all things in being, or coming into being, are carried past and swept away. Existence is like a river in ceaseless flow, its actions a constant succession of change, its causes innumerable in their variety: scarcely anything stands still, even what is most immediate. Reflect too on the yawning gulf of past and future time, in which all things vanish. So in all this it must be folly for anyone to be puffed with ambition, racked in struggle, or indignant at his lot — as if this was anything lasting or likely to trouble him for long.
sections.chinese: 当时常思量：一切存有之物、或正在生成之物，其被裹挟而过、席卷而逝之速度何其迅疾。存在如一条奔流不息之河，其诸行动变化迭更不休，其诸般原因繁复不可计数：几乎没有一物静止不动，即使那最为切近当下者。也思量那过去与未来时间之张开鸿渊，所有事物都消逝于其中。如此看来，在此一切之中，人若为野心所膨胀、为争夺所折磨、或为自身际遇而愤愤不平——仿佛这些能长久持续或能长久搅扰他一般——必是愚妄。

sections.english: Think of the whole of existence, of which you are the tiniest part; think of the whole of time, in which you have been assigned a brief and fleeting moment; think of destiny — what fraction of that are you?
sections.chinese: 思那存有之整体，你仅为其最微末之一部分；思那时间之整体，你仅被分配了一短暂而飞逝之刹那；思那命运——你是它的何等微小之一分？

sections.english: Another does wrong. What is that to me? Let him see to it: he has his own disposition, his own action. I have now what universal nature wishes me to have now, and I do what my own nature wishes me to do now.
sections.chinese: 他人做错事。那与我何干？让他自去理会：他有他自己的性情，他自有他自己的作为。我此刻则拥有宇宙自然所愿我此刻拥有之物，我则做我自身本性愿我此刻所做之事。

sections.english: The directing and sovereign part of your soul must stay immune to any current in the flesh, either smooth or troubled, and keep its independence: it must define its own sphere and confine those affections to the parts they affect.
sections.chinese: 你灵魂中主导与统御之部分，必须对肉身中一切流动——无论其平和或骚乱——保持免疫，守护其独立：它必须划定自己的领域，并将那些感受局限于它们所影响的相应部分。

sections.english: 'Live with the gods.' He lives with the gods who consistently shows them his soul content with its lot, and performing the wishes of that divinity, that fragment of himself which Zeus has given each person to guard and guide him. In each of us this divinity is our mind and reason.
sections.chinese: 「与诸神同住。」凡恒常向诸神示现一己之灵魂满足于其所分配之一切、且执行那神性之愿望的人——那神性即宙斯赋予每人以护卫并引导他自己的、己身之碎片——便是与诸神同住者。在我等每人之中，此一神性便是我们之心智与理性。

sections.english: Are you angry with the man who smells like a goat, or the one with foul breath? What will you have him do? That's the way his mouth is, that's the way his armpits are, so it is inevitable that they should give out odours to match. 'But the man is endowed with reason', you say, 'and if he puts his mind to it he can work out why he causes offence.' Well, good for you! So you too are no less endowed with reason: bring your rationality, then, to bear on his rationality — show him, tell him. If he listens, you will cure him, and no need for anger. Neither hypocrite nor whore.
sections.chinese: 你生那气味如山羊之人的气吗，或那口有秽息者？你要他怎样呢？他的嘴就是那样的，他之腋下便是那样的，故不可免地，散发的气味也就与之相配。「可是这人身秉理性」，你说道，「若他用心想过，便能明白为何他会惹人反感。」不错，说得对！那么你也不缺理性：便用你的理性来作用于他的理性——明示他，告诉他。若他听从，你便治愈了他，也无需动怒。既非伪君子，也非娼妓。

sections.english: You can live here in this world just as you intend to live when you have left it. But if this is not allowed you, then you should depart life itself — but not as if this were some misfortune. 'The fire smokes and I leave the house.' Why think this any big matter? But as long as no such thing drives me out, I remain a free man and no one will prevent me doing what I wish to do: and my wish is to follow the nature of a rational and social being.
sections.chinese: 你可以在此世中如此生活，正如你意欲在辞别此生之后那般生活。但若情形不容许你如此，那你便当辞别生命本身——但勿如遭遇祸殃一般。「屋子冒烟了，我离开这间屋。」何必视此为大事？然而，只要没有这等事将我驱赶出去，我便仍是一个自由人，无人能阻我做我所愿做之事：而我所愿的，乃是遵循一个理性且社会性存在者之本性。

sections.english: The intelligence of the Whole is a social intelligence. Certainly it has made the lower for the sake of the higher, and set the higher in harmony with each other. You can see how it has subordinated some creatures, coordinated others, given each its proper place, and brought together the superior beings in unity of mind.
sections.chinese: 宇宙整体之理智，是一种社会性之理智。它确然将低者造为高者之缘故，并使高者彼此和谐相处。你可见它是如何将某些造物置于下位，将另些造物并列协动，赋予每者以恰当之位，并将那优越的存在者们汇聚于心灵之合中。

sections.english: How have you behaved up to now towards gods, parents, brother, wife, children, teachers, tutors, friends, relations, servants? Has your principle up to now with all of these been 'say no evil, do no evil'? Remind yourself what you have been through and had the strength to endure; that the story of your life is fully told and your service completed; how often you have seen beauty, disregarded pleasure and pain, forgone glory, and been kind to the unkind.
sections.chinese: 至今为止，你对诸神、父母、兄弟、妻子、孩子、师长、保傅、朋友、亲族、仆役，行为如何？至今为止，你于这一切人的原则，是否乃是「不出恶语、不为恶行」？提醒自己：你经历过何等事，有力量承受过何等事；你生命的故事已全然讲完，你的服役已然完成；你多少次看见过美，漠视过乐与苦，放弃过荣耀，并以仁善待不善者。

sections.english: Why do unskilled and ignorant minds confound the skilful and the wise? Well, what is the mind of true skill and wisdom? It is the mind which knows the beginning and the end, and knows the Reason which informs all of existence and governs the Whole in appointed cycles through all eternity.
sections.chinese: 为何无技艺与无知之心灵，会困惑那有技艺与有智慧者？那么，什么才是真正的技艺与智慧之心灵？那便是知晓开端与终局、知晓那贯透一切存有之理性、并知晓那在指定之周期中于一切永恒里统御整体之理性的心灵。

sections.english: You can always ensure the right current to your life if you can first follow the right path — if, that is, your judgements and actions follow the path of reason. There are two things common to the souls of all rational creatures, god or man: they are immune to any external impediment, and the good they seek resides in a just disposition and just action, with this the limit of their desire.
sections.chinese: 你若能先遵循那正路——即，你的判断与行动皆遵循理性之途——便总能保证你生命之流向正直。有两事为一切理性造物、不论神或人之灵魂所共有：它们不受任何外在阻碍之影响；且它们所寻求之善好在于正直之性向与正直之行动，以此为它们欲望之界限。

sections.english: If this is no wrongdoing of mine, nor the result of any wrong done to me, and if the community is not harmed, then why do I let it trouble me? And what is the harm that can be done to the community?
sections.chinese: 若此事非我之过错，亦非我受任何不义侵害之所导致，且若共同体亦未受伤害，那我又为何任其困扰于我？究竟什么事能对共同体造成伤害？

sections.english: Don't let the impression of other people's grief carry you away indiscriminately. Help them, yes, as best you can and as the case deserves, even if their grief is for the loss of something indifferent: but do not imagine their loss as any real harm — that is the wrong way of thinking. Rather, you should be like the old man in the play who reclaimed at the end his foster-child's favourite toy, never forgetting that it was only a toy.
sections.chinese: 勿让对他人悲伤之印象不加分别地席卷你而去。帮助他们，固然——尽你所能，亦如情势所应得，纵使他们之悲伤是因失去了某件无足轻重之物：但不要将他们的损失想象为任何真正的伤害——那是错误之思维。相反，你当如同戏剧中的那位老人，在终场时将他的养子心爱的玩具索回，心里从未忘记那只是玩具而已。

sections.english: 'There was a time when I met luck at every turn.' But luck is the good fortune you determine for yourself: and good fortune consists in good inclinations of the soul, good impulses, good actions.
sections.chinese: 「曾几何时，我处处逢遇好运。」然而，运气乃是你为自己所决定之好运：而好运取决于灵魂之良好倾向、良好冲动、良好行动。
